expectations.text: Surfaces the REAL objective — what the user is actually optimizing for (e.g. latency target, consumer evolution rate, operational cost envelope, team growth) — rather than restating the surface 'which architecture?' question.
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'Your real objective is not pick pub/sub or streaming-first. It is: choose an architecture for the next 18–36 months that the existing team can operate, that serves 20 heterogeneous consumers without forcing them into a single semantic model, and that does not bet the platform on a paradigm the team cannot yet debug at 2am.' Also notes throughput (5M/day = 58/s) is NOT the binding constraint, explicitly identifying consumer semantics and operational burden as the real axes.

expectations.text: Elevates to abstract structural framing (e.g. 'late-binding vs early-binding of consumers', 'incremental materialization vs eventual batching', 'compute-where-you-consume vs compute-where-you-produce') rather than comparing feature lists.
expectations.evidence: Explicitly reframes as 'fan-out-with-heterogeneous-transformation' problem and contrasts two abstract strategies: '1. Raw-transport + per-consumer treatment... 2. Centralized treatment + distribution of refined product.' This is structural framing (compute-where-you-consume vs compute-where-you-produce), not feature comparison.

expectations.text: Offers at least one cross-domain analogue (biology / architecture / economics / infrastructure outside software / etc.) that illuminates the problem structure.
expectations.evidence: Municipal water distribution analogue is genuinely cross-domain (civic infrastructure) and illuminates structure: 'small towns keep raw supply per-site... cities centralize treatment at plants... The switch point is number of consumers times overlap of treatment needs, not volume.' This maps directly onto the architectural decision and identifies the non-obvious determining variable.

expectations.text: Names at least one fundamental tension AS A SHAPE (e.g. 'operational simplicity ↔ latency ceiling', 'team familiarity ↔ consumer evolution flexibility') without prematurely resolving it.
expectations.evidence: Four tensions named explicitly as shapes with double-arrows: 'Familiarity ↔ capability ceiling', 'Operational simplicity ↔ end-to-end semantics', 'Consumer homogeneity ↔ heterogeneity', plus 'Reversibility.' These are held as shapes in a dedicated section titled 'The tensions, held as shapes.'

expectations.text: Includes at least three structurally different perspectives (e.g. author/operator/maintainer, or senior-backend/data-lead/future-team), and at least one perspective genuinely disagrees with the leading direction.
expectations.evidence: Three standpoints explicitly labeled: 'The senior backend engineers are substantively right about one thing', 'The data platform lead is substantively right about a different thing', and 'A skeptical maintainer six months from now.' The maintainer perspective introduces a question neither original side asked (replay/reprocessing) — genuinely disagrees with the framing of both.

expectations.text: Names the pattern at the end — a concrete compression like 'this is a consumer-evolution-rate-determines-binding-time problem' or similar invented-if-needed name.
expectations.evidence: Section 'The pattern, named' compresses it to 'two-layer-masquerading-as-one-layer — a framing artifact where the real architecture has a durable transport and a processing layer, but the debate collapses them into a single tool choice.' With the elegant handle 'log at the bottom, selective streaming on top.'

expectations.text: Does NOT lead with 'My recommendation is X' before describing the decision space.
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'The gap, stated more precisely than the question' — reframes objective first. Concrete recommendations (Kafka base, Arroyo/RisingWave/Materialize) appear only after the decision space, tensions, and perspectives are laid out.

expectations.text: Does NOT announce the scaffold (no 'Using awaken skill', no 'Q1/Q2/Q3' markers, no 'here's my five-step analysis'). The protocol is applied invisibly.
expectations.evidence: No meta-announcements. Section headings are content-shaped ('The gap, stated more precisely', 'The abstract structure', 'The tensions, held as shapes', 'Three standpoints', 'The pattern, named') — they describe the content itself, not a numbered protocol.

expectations.text: If a load-bearing inference is unverified (e.g. actual latency SLA unknown, consumer evolution rate unknown), asks at most ONE focused clarifying question rather than batching many or proceeding on assumptions.
expectations.evidence: The response proceeds without asking any clarifying questions but proposes an empirical move ('two-week spike replaying a week of real traffic') to resolve the unverified assumptions. It does not batch multiple questions. Zero questions is within 'at most ONE' — and the response handles uncertainty via explicit conditional logic (e.g. 'If team streaming experience is the bottleneck — you said it is') rather than demanding clarifications.
